title: Tortilla Chips 300g

drivers.name: Price increase (3.7%)
drivers.evidence: Two prior weeks with same price: sales dropped 15% and 39% vs baseline; noise-adjusted average drop ~20%, shrunk to -15% for confidence.

drivers.name: Competitor opening across the street
drivers.evidence: No direct data, but plausible demand loss from competition; consistent with similar market events; shrunk to -10% due to uncertainty.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 124.2. A 3.7% price increase to $3.97 is likely to reduce demand. Past price hikes (2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) saw sales drop to 106 and 75 units (vs baseline 124.2), implying a ~20% demand reduction. The competitor opening across the street adds downward pressure, with no direct data but plausible substitution risk. No promotion or event is scheduled. The classical model suggests no uplift, but this overlooks the price increase and new competitor. Evidence is moderate (2 price spikes, one new competitor), so shrink toward 1.0. Median adjustment: -15%.

  median 124.2 | 5%-95%: 77.8 - 200.0 | 10%-90%: 89.2 - 170.0

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-29% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
